title: S2-Hammer V1.9 vs V3.2 — gap report
question: Reading the RS-XAUUSD-20260727-006 (V1.9) and -007 (V3.2) fail-pattern reports, where do the two S2 versions diverge on 30-minute timing, fail-type share, BB zone, DXY regime, and MTF alignment?
hypothesis: S2 evolved from a Pullback-style V1.9 signal to a Hammer-candle-style V3.2 signal (different entry rule, not only a parameter tweak), so deltas are expected and must not be read as a like-for-like backtest of the same rules across time.

findings.title: V3.2 outperforms V1.9 on every headline metric
findings.detail: WR +6.06pp (47.13% vs 41.07%), PF +0.512 (2.047 vs 1.535), on 67 fewer trades — fewer, higher-quality signals.

findings.title: MTF counter-trend penalty shrank sharply
findings.detail: The 4H-bearish win-rate gap narrowed from 4.76pp (V1.9) to 1.47pp (V3.2) — the Hammer-candle entry is less exposed to counter-trend risk than the Pullback entry was.

findings.title: time_bleed share grew, not shrank
findings.detail: time_bleed rose from 53.8% to 57.8% of losses — V3.2 did not fix the strategy's core failure mode (dragging losers), it just has fewer losses overall.

findings.title: Both versions are low-n; V3.2 more so
findings.detail: V1.9 n=224, V3.2 n=157. Most 30-minute-slot and subgroup cells are single-digit-to-teens for V3.2; S2 V3.2 OOS confidence is limited. Treat every delta here as descriptive.

findings.title: Different entry rules confound every delta
findings.detail: V1.9 (Pullback) and V3.2 (Hammer-candle) are different signal implementations, not the same rule at two parameter settings — see the .pine source files for exact differences. Deltas may reflect the rule change, not a timing/regime effect.

card_summary: What changed between S2 V1.9 and V3.2, and what did not.
